dimension_note: Wheelbase 100 in (2540 mm), track 56 in (1422 mm), 30 in wheels (Wikipedia). Frame width, heights, pivots and the steering layout are assumptions.
suspension_note: Transverse semi-elliptic spring on each beam axle (Wikipedia). Each axle is located by a ball: the front by a wishbone to a ball under the crankcase, the rear by the torque tube's ball behind the transmission. So both axles swing and roll about their balls; the springs carry the load.
steering_note: Left-hand drive. The Model T's 4:1 reduction is a planetary set under the wheel and its pitman is on the column's foot; here the reduction is the shared joint coupling and the pitman turns on a short vertical shaft in a bracket outboard of the left rail, clear of the wishbone rods. The drag link runs at the front axle's roll-axis height (0.386 m) to keep roll steer small, the lesson from 009.

shock_absorbers.note: Aftermarket Hartford-type friction shock absorbers (stage 'shocks' only): a scissor per corner whose knee is clamped between friction discs. 40 N m of knee friction gives about 190 N at each wheel (the scissor turns ~4.8 rad of knee angle per metre of axle travel near ride height). Arm length, mounting and friction are assumptions; real units were adjusted by a star nut.
